source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: While the nurse measures the fundal height of a client at 36 weeks' gestation lying flat, the client becomes pale and lightheaded. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Raise her legs on two pillows
Turn her onto her left side
Have her breathe into a paper bag
questions.rationale: Late in pregnancy, the uterus can compress the inferior vena cava and aorta when the client lies supine (supine hypotension syndrome). Turning her to the left side, or wedging the right hip, relieves the compression.
explanations: Raising the legs does not lift the uterus off the vena cava.
Correct: the left lateral position relieves vena cava compression.
This treats hyperventilation, not supine hypotension.
Continuing keeps the compression going.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 243)
questions.quote: Compression of the inferior vena cava and aorta by the uterus may cause supine hypotension syndrome (vena cava syndrome) late in pregnancy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client pregnant with twins comes for a prenatal checkup. Which complication should the nurse monitor for as a PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Two fetuses demand more iron, so maternal anemia is common and is the priority concern. Twin pregnancies tend to end preterm, not post-term.
explanations: Hemorrhoids can occur but are a lower priority.
Twin pregnancies usually end in preterm birth.
Correct: iron demand from two fetuses causes anemia.
This is not a typical priority problem of a twin pregnancy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 244)
questions.quote: Maternal anemia often occurs in twin pregnancies because of a greater demand for iron by the fetuses.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why does the nurse closely monitor the weight, vital signs, and fluid status of a pregnant client with rheumatic heart disease?
options: Pregnancy raises blood volume and cardiac output
Pregnancy slows the maternal heart rate
Blood volume drops in the third trimester
questions.rationale: Blood volume rises during pregnancy, increasing cardiac output (stroke volume × heart rate). A diseased heart may not meet this added workload and can decompensate.
explanations: Correct: the extra volume and output strain a diseased heart.
Heart rate increases in pregnancy.
Stroke volume increases with higher blood volume.
Blood volume peaks late in pregnancy; it does not drop.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 245)
questions.quote: Pregnancy taxes the circulating system of every woman because the blood volume increases, which causes the cardiac output to increase.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client with diabetes at 36 weeks' gestation has had reactive nonstress tests for 3 weeks. Today the test is nonreactive after 40 minutes. What should the nurse prepare for next?
options: Sending her home to repeat the test in 2 days
questions.rationale: A nonreactive NST needs further evaluation, and the contraction stress test is the next step. There is not enough data to justify immediate delivery, and waiting 2 days may endanger the fetus.
explanations: Delay may put the fetus at risk.
Data do not yet justify emergency surgery.
Data do not yet justify immediate induction.
Correct: a CST further assesses fetal well-being.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: A contraction stress test is the next test needed to further assess the fetal status.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client with gestational hypertension is admitted in early active labor. Which finding does the nurse MOST expect?
questions.rationale: Elevated blood pressure is the major sign of gestational hypertension. As it progresses, reflexes may become brisk, urine output falls, and fetal heart rate variability decreases.
explanations: Urine output tends to decrease.
Correct: hypertension is the defining finding.
Reflexes become hyperactive as the disease progresses.
Fluid retention leads to weight gain, not loss.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 211)
questions.quote: The major manifestation of gestational hypertension is increased blood pressure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A laboring client has sickle cell anemia. Which nursing action helps prevent a sickling crisis during labor?
options: Pushing early in the first stage
questions.rationale: Labor raises oxygen demand, which a client with sickle cell anemia may not meet. Oxygen and IV hydration lower the risk of crisis.
explanations: Hydration helps prevent sickling, so fluids are not restricted.
Early pushing is exhausting and inappropriate.
Correct: oxygen meets the higher demands of labor.
Lying flat does not prevent sickling and may compress the vena cava.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Administering oxygen will prevent sickle cell crisis during labor.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.situation: Ana, a 24-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks, is in active labor on an oxytocin infusion. The nurse is watching the fetal monitor tracing.
questions.stem: The tracing shows late decelerations. The nurse understands that these are caused by:
questions.rationale: Late decelerations come from reduced blood flow and oxygen transfer through the placenta during contractions, causing fetal hypoxemia. Oxygen and repositioning are needed.
explanations: Head compression causes early decelerations.
Cord compression causes variable decelerations.
Correct: late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency.
Sleep cycles reduce variability; they do not cause late decelerations.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 176)
questions.quote: Late decelerations are caused by uteroplacental insufficiency

questions.subject: NP II
questions.situation: Ana, a 24-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks, is in active labor on an oxytocin infusion. The nurse is watching the fetal monitor tracing.
questions.stem: Which nursing measure helps prevent fetal heart rate decelerations during Ana's labor?
options: Keep her lying flat on her back
questions.rationale: Side-lying and upright positions (walking, standing, squatting) improve venous return and uterine blood flow. Lying supine compresses the vena cava.
explanations: The supine position reduces placental blood flow.
More oxytocin can overstimulate the uterus.
Walking is an upright position that helps.
Correct: these positions improve venous return and placental flow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: Side-lying and upright positions such as walking, standing, and squatting can improve venous return and encourage effective uterine activity.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Twelve hours after a vaginal delivery, where does the nurse expect to palpate the fundus if involution is progressing normally?
options: At the level of the umbilicus
Midway between the umbilicus and symphysis
questions.rationale: Within 6 to 12 hours after birth the fundus rises to the umbilicus, stays there about a day, then descends about one fingerbreadth daily. It is no longer palpable by about day 10.
explanations: Correct: the fundus is at the umbilicus at 6 to 12 hours.
This is where the fundus sits right after the placenta is delivered.
This level is reached several days later.
The uterus is no longer palpable only by about 10 days.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 536)
questions.quote: Within 6 to12 hours after birth, the fundus of the uterus rises to the level of the umbilicus.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: On the second postpartum day, which lochia does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Lochia rubra is dark red and lasts from delivery to about day 3. Lochia serosa (pinkish-brown) follows, then lochia alba (white to yellowish).
explanations: Serosa begins after about day 3.
Alba appears in the later weeks.
Alba appears in the later weeks.
Correct: rubra lasts from delivery to about day 3.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 542)
questions.quote: Lochia rubra is dark red in color. It occurs from delivery to 3 days postpartum

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which postpartum client has the HIGHEST risk of puerperal infection?
options: A client with a 6-hour labor and spontaneous vaginal birth
A client with a history of two miscarriages
A client with cesarean birth after prolonged rupture of membranes
A client who delivered twins vaginally
questions.rationale: Risk factors include cesarean birth, prolonged rupture of membranes, prolonged labor, many vaginal examinations, trauma, retained placental fragments, and past infections.
explanations: A short labor with vaginal birth is low risk.
Past miscarriages are not a risk factor.
Correct: cesarean birth and prolonged rupture are major risk factors.
Twin vaginal delivery alone is not a listed risk factor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 251)
questions.quote: Risk factors associated with puerperal infection include a history of previous infections, excessive number of vaginal examinations, cesarean births, prolonged rupture of the membranes

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A postpartum client with heart disease is told to call the nurse before getting out of bed or caring for her baby. What is the reason for this instruction?
options: To promote bonding with the newborn
To reduce stress on her heart
To allow the perineum to heal
questions.rationale: Right after delivery, fluid shifts from the tissues back into the circulation and hormones change, adding stress to the heart. The priority is to limit cardiac workload.
explanations: Bonding matters but is not the reason for this instruction.
Correct: fluid shifts after birth add cardiac stress.
This does not address the cardiac risk.
Perineal healing is not the main concern here.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 705)
questions.quote: Hormonal changes and fluid shifts from extravascular tissues to the circulatory system cause additional stress on cardiac functioning.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which finding in a term newborn increases the risk of developing jaundice?
questions.rationale: As a cephalhematoma is reabsorbed, the broken-down red cells add to the bilirubin load. A negative Coombs test means no antibody-mediated hemolysis.
explanations: Correct: reabsorbed blood increases bilirubin.
Rh incompatibility involves an Rh-negative mother and Rh-positive infant, not the reverse.
Normal birth weight is not a risk factor.
A negative Coombs test shows no immune hemolysis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 174)
questions.quote: Enclosed hemorrhage, such as with cephalhematoma, predisposes the newborn to jaundice

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The mother's hepatitis B surface antigen test is positive. Which does the nurse anticipate for the newborn?
options: Hepatitis B vaccine and HBIG within 12 hours
Repeat maternal test before any newborn treatment
questions.rationale: Infants of HBsAg-positive mothers receive both the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours of birth. Antibiotics do not treat viral infection.
explanations: Breastfeeding is not prohibited when the infant is immunized.
Antibiotics do not act against hepatitis B virus.
Correct: vaccine plus HBIG gives active and passive protection.
Delaying protection increases the risk of infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 237)
questions.quote: the neonate should receive the hepatitis vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours after birth.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which medication is applied to a newborn's eyes to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum?
questions.rationale: Erythromycin 0.5% eye ointment is effective against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis, which the newborn can acquire in the birth canal.
explanations: Penicillin eye drops are not the standard prophylaxis.
Correct: erythromycin covers gonococcal and chlamydial infection.
Vitamin K is given IM to prevent bleeding.
Silver sulfadiazine is a burn cream.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 250)
questions.quote: Ophthalmic erythromycin 0.5% ointment is a broad-spectrum antibiotic and is used prophylactically to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 3-day-old preterm neonate has respiratory distress syndrome. Which finding shows the condition is improving?
options: Edema of the hands and feet
questions.rationale: As alveoli open, lung fluid moves into the bloodstream and is excreted by the kidneys, so normal urination (2 to 5 mL/kg/hour) is an early sign of improvement.
explanations: Edema appears early in RDS and does not show improvement.
Correct: increased voiding is an early sign of improvement.
Tachypnea shows ongoing distress.
Grunting is a sign of respiratory distress.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: normal urination is an early sign that the neonate’s respiratory condition is improving

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which safety teaching is MOST appropriate for the mother of a 1-month-old infant?
options: Place the baby on the back to sleep
questions.rationale: At 1 month, the key instructions are back-to-sleep positioning and never shaking the baby. Outlet covers, locked chemicals, and gates matter once the infant starts moving around, at about 6 months.
explanations: Correct: back-sleeping reduces the risk of sudden infant death.
Outlets become a hazard when the infant is mobile.
Poisoning becomes a risk once the infant explores.
Stairs become a hazard with crawling.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 693)
questions.quote: place the infant on his or her back to sleep

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is the HIGHEST priority in the care of a hospitalized toddler?
options: Adapting the toddler to hospital routines
questions.rationale: A toddler's mobility, curiosity, and the unfamiliar environment create a high risk of injury. Consistency and play matter, but safety comes first.
explanations: Important for separation anxiety, but safety comes first.
Toddlers do better when their home routines are kept.
Helpful, but not the top priority.
Correct: safety is the highest priority.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 732)
questions.quote: protection from injury is the highest priority.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which personal-social milestone should the nurse tell a mother to expect in her 3-year-old?
questions.rationale: A 3-year-old puts on articles of clothing, brushes teeth with help, washes hands, knows their own name, and begins to take turns.
explanations: Tying shoelaces is a skill of about 5 to 6 years.
Correct: dressing in simple clothing is expected at 3.
Bicycle riding comes at school age.
Printing a name comes at about 5 to 6 years.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 813)
questions.quote: putting on articles of clothing; brushing teeth with help
